C005.verdict: LENS 1 (data): not refuted. Every input exists in real time. Per-call context (input+cache_read+cache_creation), output tokens and api_calls/turn are already in State (src/metrics/usage.rs Turn{api_calls, usage, context_size, first_call_prefix}); prices come from pricing.toml (cache_read defaults to 0.1x input, fable-5-1 overridden to 0.25 $/MTok — matches the official CHANGELOG 2.1.257 note in the docs report). The window is live in the status shim (~/.cctop/status/*.json: context_window_size=1000000 for opus-5, sonnet-5, fable-5-1; 200000 for haiku) and the official model-config doc says native-1M models auto-compact at ~967k with no price premium above 200k, which is why two sessions ran to 921k/953k with 0 compactions. The 'clean end' inputs: (a) last assistant block is text — in the transcript for 657/669 turns; (b) system turn_duration.pendingBackgroundAgentCount — the 2.1.269 binary builds it (`subtype:"turn_duration",durationMs:e,budgetTokens..,messageCount:r,pendingBackgroundAgentCount:s,pendingWorkflowCount:d`) but the key is omitted when 0: only 13 of 453 turn_duration lines carry it (all =1), and turn_duration itself exists for only 449/669 turns, and cctop's SystemLine (src/transcript.rs:295-310) does not parse it; (c) Stop.background_tasks[] is in the d.ts (StopHookInput, plugin/.claude/types/claude-code.d.ts:6771-6781) and survives cctop's spool filter (hooks.rs:72-77 only drops tool_response/tool_input/transcript_path); the live spool has 45 Stop events (31 with 0 tasks, 14 with 1) — optional source, needs the cctop hooks installed. The candidate's 'status context_window.current_usage (unparsed)' is a real key in the status file (current_usage{input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,output_tokens}) but is redundant: status.rs already parses total_input_tokens/context_window_size and the transcript gives the same figures per call. LENS 2 (actionability): not refuted, but the estimate needs three corrections. Re-running the scratchpad scripts (c005.py, c005turns.py, c005_after.py over main_all.jsonl, 6543 priced calls, $992 list price, 2026-08-12..09-12): calls >300k = 25.5% of calls and 51.6% of spend (candidate 26.5%/53.6%, minor drift); $/call median 0.183 (300-400k) and 0.311 (>400k) vs 0.056-0.074 below 200k; $/turn median 1.26/2.15 vs 0.27; cache-read cost of the portion above 300k = $176/month = 17.8%; 6 sessions >400k, 12 >300k; top-5% turns: ctx p50 412k, 30 calls, 40% of spend. NOT reproduced: 'p50 calls per long run (32)' — long runs (>=10 calls) have p50 19 calls; 30 is the top-5% figure, so the 'next 30 calls' projection overstates by ~1.6x for a typical run. Honest benefit: $176 is the cost of all context above 300k, i.e. an upper bound assuming a free reset. Per session (c005_after) the spend after first crossing 300k is $363 across 12 sessions and the upper-bound read saving vs a 100k context is $229; median turns after crossing = 4, so in 8 of 12 sessions the nudge arrives with <=5 turns left and 83% of the saving sits in 3 sessions (a6d60f35 $91, e370b5c1 $61, e3346d84 $38). A fresh session starts at 26-65k (first-call ctx p10/p50/p90 = 26/45/65k), and the hand-off re-reads files, so a realistic capture is ~50-60% of the bound: ~$110-140/month list price, ~11-14% of spend — still the biggest single lever, but not 18.5%. Bigger caveat: this owner is a subscriber (all 8 status files carry rate_limits.five_hour/seven_day; the docs report C05 says Max includes Opus 1M), so the $ are notional; the lever is plan usage. That is still real — official costs.md lists 'long context re-read every request' as the first reason usage climbs and /usage flags 'long context' at >=10% of recent usage — but only 4 rate-limit hits appear in a month of transcripts, so the pain is headroom, not hard stops; the line must be phrased in usage share/limit terms for subscribers (C024). Duplication: the action text is identical to A06/A18 ('hand-off note, start fresh'), but neither fires in this regime: A18 needs >70% of the window (700k on 1M) and 3h, A06 needs compactions (0 in 11 of 12 sessions). So C005 fills a real gap and should be implemented as the metric plus a widened A18 trigger rather than a 19th rule. False positives: the clean-end gate barely filters (134/140 >300k turn ends are clean), so the +100k re-fire is the only limiter (a6d60f35: 33 qualifying turn ends, 5 fires) — acceptable for a metric line, marginal for an alert; a person doing one long deliberate task will see it 3-5 times. /clear mid-task loses state, so lead with /compact <focus>. Wording: the proposed 'ctx 420k · $0.23/call · ~$2.6/turn (vs $0.41 at < 100k) · next 30 calls ~ $6.3' is 74 chars, over 56. Side finding: 37 calls >300k rewrote >100k cache tokens (17.4M tokens, ~$109 at opus write rates) after idle gaps — that is A02's domain and a separate, larger per-incident cost than the per-call read.
C005.corrections: Trigger: keep every-tick metric; escalate on ctx > 300k AND last assistant block is text with stop_reason end_turn (transcript, 656/669 turns) — do not depend on turn_duration.pendingBackgroundAgentCount (absent for 1/3 of turns, key omitted when 0, unparsed); treat absence as 0 and add it to SystemLine as Option<u32>; use Stop.background_tasks.length == 0 only when the hook spool is live. Projection: use the session's own p50 calls/turn over long runs (19 calls at p50 for runs >=10 calls; 30 only for the top 5%), never a fixed 32. Benefit: state '~$110-140/month realistic (upper bound $176-229)', 11-14% of spend, concentrated in ~3 sessions/month; for subscribers (this owner: rate_limits present) render as '% of 5h/7d limit per turn' not $, e.g. 'ctx 420k: each call re-reads 420k · 5h 62%'. Data source: drop 'context_window.current_usage' — use State.agg.turns[].context_size and status.context_window_size (already parsed); window default 967k auto-compact on native-1M models per docs. Rule mapping: implement as a Context-panel/coach metric and widen A18's trigger (ctx > 300k absolute on a 1M window OR > 70%) instead of a new rule; keep A06 untouched. Action order: '/compact <focus>' first (cheap on 1M: one ~400k cache-read pass), '/clear + 5-line hand-off' second. Wording (<=56 cols, 2 lines): 'ctx 420k → $0.23/call, ~$2.6/turn (was $0.4 <100k)' / 'clean stop: /compact <focus> or hand-off + /clear'. Pricing: fable-5-1 cache read is $0.25/MTok (0.025x), so the escalation is 4x weaker on Fable — show per-model figures from pricing.toml, not a 10% rule of thumb.

C006.verdict: LENS 1 (data availability): NOT refuted. Every input exists in real time from the tailed transcript: src/tools.rs:145 sets Call.result_tokens_est = len(r.text())/4 on the user tool_result line (transcript.rs:168-178, text blocks only, images ignored); the full tool_use input is already parsed as serde Value (transcript.rs:223-228), so input_tokens_est is a one-line addition rather than a real C013 dependency; cache_read price is in pricing.toml (0.1x input default, fable-5-1 = 0.25) and reaches State via CostTracker::new(pricing) (state.rs:314-316); compactions are tracked (state.rs:148, 399). Gap: src/baseline.rs Baseline has no calls-per-session field — figures() computes calls = stats.calls.len() (line 69) but only for error_rate; a median must be added. Re-derived on the current 90-session main-thread corpus (scratchpad/main_all.jsonl): p95 tool result = 2,109 tokens (not 1.8k), n>=1.8k = 390 results = 53% of tool-result tokens, calls/session median 33 (candidate's 43 is the older 77-session anatomy figure). LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED as a per-call live nudge. (1) The remaining-calls estimate max(median - calls_so_far, 10) lands within 2x of the actual remaining API calls for only 38% of large results (ratio p25 0.21, median 1.03, p75 1.70), so the displayed '$0.30 over the rest of the session' figure is wrong by >2x in 62% of firings; 22.5% of large results have <10 calls left (tax ~0) — already at the 1-in-5 line by itself. (2) The advice is already-done or wrong for a large share: 54% of large Reads are followed by an Edit/Write of the same file within 40 calls (legitimate read-before-edit), 16% are already ranged; 38% of large Bash results already pipe through head/tail/grep; the program mix of large Bash results is cat 81 (30%), sed 45 (16%, mostly `sed -n` ranged reads under bash-first auto mode), git 33 (diff/log), gh 13, python3 9 — only the cat/ls/find/unfiltered-grep group (~40%) fits 'narrow the command'. Combined false-positive rate is well above 1 in 5. (3) Frequency: median 3 large results per session, p75 6, p90 10, max 18; median 5 per hour, p75 25; 68% of large results have another within 3 API calls, so a per-call transient line churns and violates the coach budget (max 1 new nudge/turn, ~6/hour, candidates.md:612). (4) Timing: the result is already in context when the nudge fires; mid-turn the person can only press Esc or queue a message, so it is not a per-call action but a turn-end retrospective. (5) It duplicates A03 (rules.rs:150-193): same action text ('Narrow the command (head, grep, Glob) or delegate'), differing only in threshold (1.8k vs 3k) and the marginal-cost framing. (6) Subscription: this user is billingType=stripe_subscription (~/.claude.json oauthAccount); costs.md line 352 confirms cached re-reads still draw plan usage, so the lever is real, but a '$' label is misleading for them. Median tax of a large result at opus-5 cache-read price is $0.054 (p75 $0.14, p90 $0.36, max $2.22) — real but small per event, which is exactly what A03's session ranking already captures.
C006.corrections: Keep the metric, drop the per-call nudge. (a) View element: add a 'ctx tax' column to the Tools top-ctx line and the Advisor ranking = tokens x expected remaining calls, shown as a lower bound ('>= 12k tok x 10 calls') or tokens-only, never a $ point estimate; for subscription accounts (oauthAccount.billingType != api) label it 'usage', not '$'. Reset expected remaining calls at compaction/clear. Add Baseline.calls_per_session (median of stats.calls.len() over 7-day sessions, src/baseline.rs figures()). (b) Fold the marginal-cost framing into A03 instead of a new rule: A03 evidence line becomes '4.4k tokens x ~N later calls (~M tok re-read)'. (c) If a coach line is wanted, tighten the trigger to: result >= 3k tokens AND tool in {Bash cat/ls/find/tree/unfiltered grep, Read without offset/limit} AND no head/tail/grep/sed -n/-m filter in the command AND no Edit/Write of that file_path in the same turn AND calls_so_far < baseline median (early-session only, where remaining calls are plausibly high) AND not within 3 calls of a previous firing; class LATER, evaluate at turn end, at most once per turn, cooldown 5 turns, self-snooze after 3 unacted. Exact user action: at the next prompt (or queued while Claude works) write 'pipe long output through tail -50 / grep; Read with offset+limit'; or Esc to interrupt when the same command is about to be repeated. Wording (<= 56 cols, 2 lines): line 1 'cat src/x.rs: 12k tok now in ctx, re-read every call'; line 2 'Next: ask for sed -n ranges / Read offset+limit'. (d) Use p95 = ~2.1k (per-user baseline) rather than a fixed 1.8k if a threshold is ever shown as 'top 5%'.

C008.verdict: LENS 1 (data availability) largely holds: every field the trigger names exists in real 2.1.269 transcripts and is written in real time on the tool-result line. `toolUseResult.file.truncatedByTokenCap` is true on 7 of 295 Read results (typed at plugin/.claude/types/claude-code.d.ts:8944, with numLines/totalLines at :8938/:8942); the `attachment.type=="read_truncation_notice"` line (7 occurrences) has keys {banner, toolUseID, type} and the banner carries "showing lines 1-N of M total (X tokens, cap 25000)"; `toolUseResult.persistedOutputPath/persistedOutputSize` appear on 33 Bash results (d.ts:8698/8700; 17 ≥ 50 KB, 6 ≥ 100 KB, max 724,550 B, all 33 files still on disk); the `<persisted-output>` stub prefix appears in 40 tool_result blocks; the MCP "exceeds maximum allowed tokens" text appears in 2 tool_results and is a literal in the binary. cctop already parses `stop_reason` (src/transcript.rs:207), keeps `tool_use_result` as raw Value (:95) and `attachment` as raw Value (:404), and its hook spool strips `tool_response` (src/hooks.rs:74) and does not forward StopFailure (hooks.rs EVENTS list, 12 events). The one unverifiable leg is the cut-off sub-trigger: `stop_reason=="max_tokens"` occurs 0 times in 13,200 assistant messages (12,220 tool_use / 968 end_turn / 7 stop_sequence / 5 null); the binary has a silent `max_output_tokens_recovery` transition plus a `query_truncated_response_recovery` companion nudge, but no such trace exists in the corpus, so its transcript shape is unknown. LENS 2 (actionability) REFUTES the candidate as a live nudge. The harness already tells the model exactly what the coach would tell the human: the PARTIAL banner literally says "Call Read with offset=N+1 limit=N for the next page, or Grep to find a specific section. Do NOT answer from this page alone" (binary string at bin.strings line 284131), and the persisted stub gives the path plus a 2 KB preview. Measured follow-through in the same turn: truncated Reads 7/7 paged with offset, 0/7 edited, and 0/7 targets were source files (2 tool-results, 5 scratch); persisted outputs 31/33 re-run narrowed with head/grep/tail, 10/33 read the persisted file, only 1/33 did neither; verify-class spills were 2/33 and both were followed up, and in both the failure markers were inside the 2 KB preview (hidden-only 0/2; the 15 "hidden-only" cases are grep/cat/git dumps where "error" is content). So a per-occurrence nudge would fire when nothing needs doing in roughly 32 of 33 spills and 7 of 7 truncations, far past the 1-in-5 ignore threshold, and the user_action ("queue read lines N-M") duplicates a follow-up the model is already issuing before the person could type. The cut-off leg has zero base rate and its benefit citation is inverted: the 2.1.269 CHANGELOG line 12 says the cache invalidation after an auto-resumed cut-off was FIXED in this very version, so there is no remaining cost to warn about. Benefit numbers are also off (7 truncations not 4; 33 spills not 25-27; 40 stubs not 123 in main transcripts) and the sample wording is ~165 chars, exceeding 2 x 56. No A01-A18 duplication (A03 will not fire on a 2 KB stub; A04 overlaps only the offset/limit phrasing).
C008.corrections: Do not ship as a per-occurrence nudge. Salvage two things. (1) Miss-only nudge, evaluated at turn end (assistant stop_reason=="end_turn" or Stop hook), firing only when BOTH: a Read result with file.truncatedByTokenCap==true (or a read_truncation_notice attachment) whose filePath is under the project cwd and not under tool-results/ or the scratchpad, AND no later Read of that filePath with offset in the same turn AND an Edit/Write/MultiEdit on that filePath occurred after the truncation; or a Bash result with persistedOutputPath and command matching a verify class (cargo test|build|check|clippy, npm/pnpm/yarn test|run, pytest, go test, make, tsc, jest, vitest, mvn, gradle, dotnet, ruff, eslint, mypy) AND no later tool call in the turn references the persistedOutputPath or pipes through head/grep/tail/rg. Observed base rate on this machine: 0/7 and about 1/33 (0/2 verify), i.e. it fires only on a real miss. Wording ≤ 56 cols x 2: "Read src/big.rs cut at 25k tok; edited without paging" / "ask: read lines 221-261 of src/big.rs, then re-check" and "cargo test spilled 724 KB; Claude never opened it" / "ask: rerun | grep -E 'FAIL|error' | head -60". Take the line numbers from the banner text ("showing lines 1-N of M total") rather than numLines/totalLines alone. (2) Move the cut-off case to an Events row, not a nudge: fire on assistant stop_reason=="max_tokens" or assistant .error=="max_output_tokens" (SDKAssistantMessageError, d.ts:6065) if ever observed, or via the optional StopFailure hook (d.ts:6764, not in cctop hooks.rs EVENTS); wording "Response hit the output-token cap and auto-resumed". Drop the "corrupted the cache" benefit line: CHANGELOG 2.1.269 line 12 records that fix as shipped. Correct the counts: 7 token-cap truncations with 7 banners, 33 persisted outputs (17 ≥ 50 KB, max 724 KB), 40 stubs in main-thread tool_results, 2 MCP over-limit errors; timeouts (13) are not part of this trigger and should be dropped or split out. C009.verdict: LENS 1 (data) holds with corrections: attachment lines carry a top-level `rendered:[{content}]` from 2.1.266 on (0 of 5,693 attachment lines before 2.1.266 have it; 174/183 on 2.1.266; 1,929/2,376 on 2.1.269), written in real time as the query loop appends them, and cctop's `Attachment` struct (src/transcript.rs:401-405, `{timestamp, attachment: Value}`) drops the key, so a ledger needs a struct change; skill_listing carries {skillCount,isInitial,names}, edited_text_file {filename,snippet}, task_reminder {content[{id,status,subject,...}],itemCount} (never `rendered`, but the binary renders it as exactly `#${id}. [${status}] ${subject}` per line, so cctop can compute it exactly rather than with the 0.28 heuristic); CLAUDE_CODE_TOTAL_TOKENS_REMINDER / settings.totalTokensReminder ('off' valid, marked @internal) exist in the binary. LENS 2 (actionability) is refuted on all three nudges and the >5k trigger: (1) skill_listing re-sends are deltas of the NEW skills only (binary: `j4s(...) -> {newSkills,isInitial}`, log 'Sending N skills via attachment (initial|dynamic)'); measured re-sends are 279-673 bytes (~70-170 tok), never 3.3k — the 13x session e3346d84 (2.1.263) cost ~2k total, not 39k, and the pattern (skillCount alternating 1/2 with identical bytes) is a dynamic/MCP skill flapping, not the user toggling plugins; on 2.1.266+ there is exactly 1 dynamic re-send across 46 sessions, so the rule never fires and when it would, the saving is ~0.5k. Note that only an API call refreshes the TTL — a slash command that does not hit the API (/cost, /context) does not. (d) Wording fits 2x56 with the corrected lines below. C012.verdict: LENS 1 (data availability): NOT refuted. Every named source exists on this machine and is live. Bash tool_use carries the full command in message.content[].input.command on 4573/4573 Bash calls in the last 30 days (jq over ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl); cctop merely clips it to 30 chars in src/tools.rs:53-80 (summarize_input -> clip(&s,30)), so the C055 dependency is a State change, not a data gap. The attachment auto_mode line exists with keys {autoModeConsentFlow, bashFirst:boolean, bashFirstSteer, bypass, steerOnly, type} (82 lines/30 days, bashFirst=true on 64). Per-API-call context (input+cache_read+cache_creation) is on every assistant line; cctop's Turn keeps only the last call's context_size (src/metrics/usage.rs:96-97,300), so 'delta ctx per run' needs a ctx snapshot at run start - trivial. The Explore agent type exists (4 agent-*.meta.json with agentType Explore; 193 workflow-subagent, 15 general-purpose) and 2.1.269 supports queued messages ('Press up to edit queued messages, Enter to send them immediately' in the binary), so the user action is real. Caveat: the '~70-270 tokens returned' figure is a corpus constant from 10 Explore calls, not live-computable. LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED as specified - the trigger point and benefit claim do not survive replay. Re-simulating the candidate's own run definition (Read/Grep/Glob/WebFetch/ToolSearch/WebSearch + Bash read-only; reset on Edit/Write/Bash-write; end on Agent; turn boundary) over 109 transcripts <=30 days: 76 runs reach length 6 (candidate says 83 - consistent) and 46 reach 8 (exact match). But 30/76 (39%) end at length 6-7, i.e. the nudge fires when at most one read-only call remains; calls remaining after call 6: p50 2, mean 3.9, p90 11. The only savable quantity - context growth AFTER the nudge - is p50 10.5k, p75 22k, p90 43k, and only 51% of runs have >=10k left; at threshold 8 remaining growth is p50 9.5k (13/46 = 28% end at 8-9). So 'runs like this add p50 49k (p90 103k)' overstates the delegable benefit ~4-5x (the bulk is already in context when the line appears), and the fire-with-nothing-to-save rate (~49% at 6) is far above the 1-in-5 bar. The p50 figures are also internally inconsistent across the source reports (PH-08 explore_runs_ge8 dctx p50 38.8k/p90 102.9k; PH-10 48.7k; my recompute 35.9k/p90 90.5k) - the candidate splices PH-10's p50 with PH-08's p90. The nudge duplicates A05 (same lever, same action; C012 is A05 made Bash-aware, current-run and retiring - A05 today keys on the session-longest run and never retires, src/advisor/rules.rs:236-273) and its second line ('That read was 5.9k tokens - use head/sed -n/grep, or Read with offset+limit') duplicates A03 (single result > 3k, rules.rs:150-190, prd-cctop.md:196) almost verbatim. The proposed wording is ~118 chars = 3 lines at 56 columns. Bash read/write ambiguity is real but tolerable: 473/4573 (10.3%) commands match both a read verb and a write indicator. Cache economics: the run's tokens are written once at full price and then re-read at 10% on every later call, so the honest unit is 'remaining growth x remaining calls x 0.1 + compaction risk', or rate-limit budget for subscription users - frame as context, not dollars. The exploration COUNTER itself (from call 1, as a strip status) is harmless and useful; it is the delegate nudge at 6 with the 49k claim that fails.
C012.corrections: (1) File C012 as the REPLACEMENT for A05 (Bash-aware classification via C055, current run not session-longest, retires when the run ends) plus a coach-strip surfacing of A03 for the >3k single-result line - not as two new rules. (2) Keep the informational counter from call 1: 'EXPLORING x6 · +23k ctx this run' (status, never a nudge). (3) Raise the delegate nudge trigger to run >= 8 AND ctx growth this run >= 20k (or >= 6 only if growth already >= 25k); with the count-only trigger at 6, 39% of fires have <=1 call left and 49% have <10k of savable growth. Optionally require the run to have crossed a turn's 3rd+ read-only burst to avoid the 19/76 runs that end at turn end (answer/review turns). (4) Replace 'runs like this add p50 49k (p90 103k)' with a live number computed from the run's own growth, and if a corpus constant is wanted use 'typically ~10k more (p90 ~45k) before the run ends' - the delegable remainder, not the whole run. Drop the '~70-270 tokens' constant (n=10). (5) Wording <=2 lines at 56 cols: line 1 'EXPLORING x8 · +31k ctx this run'; line 2 "Esc → 'delegate the rest to an Explore agent'". For the A03 line: 'Last read 5.9k tok · ask for head/sed -n/offset+limit'. (6) Classifier: treat the 10.3% ambiguous read+write Bash commands as run-resetting (write), not read-only, so runs are not inflated; keep the 'other' class (ops/verify/mcp) as non-breaking as the candidate does. (7) Benefit framing: context/rate-limit units ('keeps ~N k out of every later request'), not $; note cache-read at 10% of input price in docs. Three sub-claims are wrong: (a) 'queued' prompts have origin.kind=human and are human-typed while Claude is busy, not idle-triggered; 'sdk' turns are Ralph/-p bot prompts (23 "Ralph agent instruction") - neither belongs in an idle trigger; (b) cross-session messages (24 lines beginning "Another Claude session") and teammate messages (39 "<\teammate-message", teamName key present) carry NO promptSource/origin at all - they must be detected by content prefix; (c) no local transcript shows an idle goal check-in (goal continuation turns appear as isMeta user lines "Stop hook feedback"), and goal_status.tokens is the goal's main-turn spend, not check-in cost - the check-in part rests on docs only (goal.md: 30 min then doubling, max 3 idle check-ins per goal, CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0 turns them off). C013.verdict: LENS 1 (data availability) NOT refuted: every input the candidate needs is in the main transcript in real time. assistant lines carry full `message.content[].tool_use.input` (not truncated: Write `input.content` alone sums to 207,661 chars/4 across the corpus, so IN->CTX per call is computable from the same Line::Assistant branch tools.rs already walks at src/tools.rs:148-170, which today keeps only a 30-char `input_summary`); `message.usage.output_tokens` is identical on every line sharing a `message.id` (4,552 multi-line ids, 0 with varying output_tokens), so the per-message denominator is safe; cctop's `Pricing::bundled()` has claude-opus-5 output $25/M and input $5/M (src/metrics/cost.rs:373-382), so "11k heredoc = $0.28 output" is arithmetically right. "Bash-first auto mode" is also detectable live: `attachment.type=="auto_mode"` lines carry `bashFirst:true, bashFirstSteer:"strict"` (64 of 84 auto_mode attachments on this machine). LENS 2 (actionability) REFUTED as specified, on three grounds. (1) The proposed action does not move the displayed metric: switching a heredoc to Write puts the identical content into `tool_use.input` (same output tokens, same context residency); the only real waste is content written twice or read back, which I measured at 218 rewrite events (121,964 tok) + 142 written-then-read targets (158,708 tok) ≈ 280k tok ≈ 5.6 % of the corpus's 5.0M output tokens (not the 1.59M / 476k the candidate implies as savings). Worse, Write on an existing file is refused with "File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it." (string in the 2.1.269 binary; 3 such errors in transcripts), so heredoc→Write for rewrites adds a Read. (2) The harness itself instructs heredocs in strict bash-first auto mode ("make file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts, rather than using the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools") — the steer is chosen by feature gate `tengu_thrifty_sonic` and only relaxed via undocumented env `CLAUDE_CODE_COZY_TEAPOT=relaxed` / settings key `tengu_cozy_teapot`; so the session trigger "heredoc writes > Write calls" (corpus: 888 heredoc calls vs 155 Write) fires in essentially every auto-mode session by design, not by user error. (3) The per-call ">= 1k tokens" trigger has an unacceptable false-positive rate: of 261 payloads >= 1k, 68 are Write (new files), 11 Edit, 8 SendMessage, 7 Agent prompts, 5 ExitPlanMode plans — ≥ 34 % are unavoidable/correct before counting first-time heredoc writes (152 of the 158 large Bash inputs are heredocs, most to fresh paths). Benefit-estimate numbers are also overstated for this machine: by chars/4 over deduplicated message ids, tool inputs are 1.51M of 5.00M output tokens (30 %, not 58 %) and Bash command text 918k (18 %, not 35 %); T09's 58 % is a chars-proportional split of output, which is a defensible but different method. Wording (~150 chars) exceeds 2 × 56 columns. Does not duplicate A01–A18, but the read-back sub-signal overlaps A04 (re-reads).

C022.verdict: LENS 1 (data): partly holds, partly wrong. Per-message tool_use count and text presence ARE computable in real time: cctop's transcript parser already deserialises AssistantBlock::{Text,Thinking,ToolUse} per assistant line and groups lines by message.id (src/transcript.rs:200-230), and usage gives ctx per call; so a "consecutive assistant messages with exactly one tool_use and no text" counter is buildable from the tailed .jsonl with no optional source. The attachment batching_reminder_sent line exists with keys {type, model, text} — but its claimed meaning is wrong: across 113 transcripts it appears 303 times (not 53/month; all 303 in 2026-09), all model=claude-fable-5-1, identical 126-char text, and it is emitted after essentially EVERY Fable tool-bearing message, including the very first tool call of a turn (session 8566721e: assistant tool call at 17:01:24, reminder at 17:01:25) and after 2-, 3- and 5-tool messages (270 single-tool, 16 two-tool, 17 three-plus; only 3 Fable tool messages lacked one). It is therefore a per-tool-result harness injection, not evidence of a serial run, and cannot serve as a trigger. LENS 2 (actionability): refuted. (a) On Fable the harness already sends the exact instruction the candidate wants the user to type ("First privately list what you need next; then request every item that doesn't depend on another's result in this one response.") after every tool result, so a user nudge is redundant there. (b) On the models where a user nudge could matter, the runs are overwhelmingly not batchable: of 174 main-chain runs of >=5 consecutive single-tool no-text messages (129 of 5-9, 19 of 10-14, 26 of >=15; models opus-5 84, sonnet-5 71, fable 14, haiku 5), 131 (75%) are >=70% Bash/Edit/Write — run-fix-run chains that must be serial (the auto-mode instruction "do your work through the Bash tool" makes single-Bash calls the norm) — and only 3 (1.7%) are mostly Read/Grep/Glob, which is exactly A05's existing trigger (>=8 consecutive Read/Grep/Glob, src/advisor/rules.rs:236). The transcript cannot tell dependent from independent Bash calls, so the nudge would fire wrongly in roughly 3 of 4 runs — far above the 1-in-5 threshold. (c) Timing: mid-turn the only keyboard action is Esc + re-prompt, which restarts the turn and re-reads the same context (net loss); the delegation advice is only useful for the next task. (d) Benefit arithmetic is directionally right (cache-read per round-trip: p50 ctx at run start 153,631 tok, p90 511,601; opus-5 cache read $0.50/M -> ~$0.08/call, fable $0.25/M -> ~$0.04/call) but the candidate counts the full run as saveable, whereas only the independent subset saves anything; and "~1.5M tok this run" style wording is 170+ chars, over 2x56. Candidate's own run counts (78) and reminder counts (53) do not match this machine (174 and 303).

C021.verdict: LENS 1 (data): mostly holds, with two material corrections. Per-turn edit counts ARE computable in real time: Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool_use lines carry input.file_path, tools::Call already has a `turn` field (src/tools.rs:33,168), and toolUseResult.structuredPatch/originalFile arrive on the following user line (497 structuredPatch results across 113 main transcripts, avg 22.8 patch lines, userModified always false). BUT (a) the clause "file-history-delta backup.version >= 8" can never fire: all 252 file-history-delta lines on this machine have backup.version == 1 (the delta is only emitted when a file is first tracked); the versions 2..28 live only in file-history-snapshot.snapshot.trackedFileBackups[path].version, which is written once per user prompt (594 snapshots, isSnapshotUpdate always false, one SNAP line immediately before each USER line) and increments once per TURN that touched the file, not per edit — so "v9" means "edited in 8 distinct turns", and it lags one turn (cross-turn only, never mid-turn). (b) In this corpus the majority of edits bypass the Edit tool: 682 Bash `sed -i`/heredoc/redirect edits vs 351 Edit + 155 Write in main transcripts (auto-mode instructs Bash editing), and per official docs (C08) Bash and subagent edits are not checkpoint-tracked, so both the version signal and the file_path count miss most of the churn unless a Bash-command regex is added. LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED as specified. Recounting the trigger on main transcripts gives 21 (turn,file) cases with >= 4 edits (max 11; candidate claimed 37/max 21), 6 files with >= 8 edits per session (max 35; claimed 15/76) and 42 E-R-E sequences (claimed 67) — the benefit estimate is ~1.5-2x inflated. Of the 21 cases, 13 are .md/.yaml/.json (PRD/progress files iterated by design in ralph loops) and 8 are code; the distribution is [4x11, 5x3, 6x2, 7x2, 10x2, 11x1], so a nudge at the 4th edit fires on a turn that stops at 4-5 edits in 14/21 (67%) — far above the 1-in-5 tolerance — and the code-only cases are [4,4,4,4,5,5,7,7], i.e. nothing beyond 7. The cross-turn "v8+ -> re-plan" rule would fire on every ralph-loop session (prd.json/progress.md are legitimately touched every story). The recommended action ("rewrite the whole file in one Write") also has a known rework cost: full-file rewrites drop content and lose the diff review that Edit gives, and for a large file the Write output tokens ($75/M Opus) can exceed the saved cache-read round trips; the round-trip saving is real only for many-edit turns on small/medium files. Not a duplicate of A04 (A04 is reads with no edit between; E-R-E is uncovered) — but as specified the false-positive rate and the inflated estimate make this a LATER-class candidate needing a much tighter trigger.
C021.corrections: Trigger: drop the file-history-delta clause (always version 1); use file-history-snapshot.trackedFileBackups[path].version only as a cross-turn "touched in N turns" signal (lag 1 turn), and only for non-doc files (exclude .md/.yaml/.json/prd*/progress*). Mid-turn: fire at >= 6 same-path Edit/MultiEdit in the current turn (tools::Call.turn), or >= 2 Edit->Read->Edit sequences on the path within the turn; count Bash edits via regex on input.command (`sed -i <path>`, `cat > <path> <<`, `> <path>`) since 682 of ~1,190 edits here are Bash. Cooldown per file per session (not 10 turns). Wording (<= 2 x 56 cols): "src/x.rs: 6 edits + 2 re-reads this turn. Ask for one Edit / that replaces the whole function." Action: prefer "one Edit covering the whole function/block" over whole-file Write (Write loses the diff and risks dropped content on files > ~300 lines). Benefit estimate: on this machine 21 turn/file cases >= 4 edits (max 11), 8 of them code (max 7), 6 files >= 8 edits per session (max 35), 42 E-R-E sequences; saving per avoided round trip = cache-read of current context (~$0.03-0.15 at 20-100k Opus) + patch/originalFile result bytes, minus the extra output tokens of the larger single edit. Drop the "v8+ -> re-plan" cross-turn nudge or gate it on code files with >= 3 turns AND a tool error/test failure in between (otherwise it fires on normal iterative PRD/progress work). Files panel column "edits this turn" is cheap and safe to add regardless.

The formula and every constant are verbatim in the 2.1.269 binary: `function On(e){...fable→10, opus→5, haiku→1, else 3}` and `function Ln(e){return(e.cached+e.uncached*10+e.cacheCreate*12.5+e.output*50)*e.modelTier}` (bin.strings offset ~28139269); `s=Ln(n)` feeds cacheMissCost/longCtxCost/sessions/buckets; thresholds Ae=1e5, Oe=150000, Le=3, we=0.5, Ie=300000, ke=4, Ne=8, Gjt=10 all present; the byte-needles the scanner uses are `"input_tokens":`, `"output_tokens":`, `"cache_creation_input_tokens":`, `"cache_read_input_tokens":`, `"model":"`, `"requestId":"`, `"isSidechain":true`. Every named source exists on this machine and is readable live from the transcript tail: Read results carry toolUseResult {type:"text", file:{filePath,content,numLines,startLine,totalLines[,truncatedByTokenCap]}} (278+7 occurrences) and {type:"file_unchanged", file:{filePath}[,source:"seeded"]} (5 occurrences, model-facing text "Wasted call — file unchanged since your last Read..." / "This file is already in your context..."); attachment.type=="edited_text_file" {type,filename,snippet} appears 126 times; Bash toolUseResult.staleReadFileStateHint (string, 93–325 chars) appears in 4 transcripts and the binary describes it as "readFileState entries whose mtime bumped during this command (set when WRITE_COMMAND_MARKERS matches)"; the 2.1.269 binary still contains tengu_file_read_reread {priorOp: seeded|edit_write|read} and the dedupe branch (gated by tengu_read_dedup_killswitch / dedupUnchangedReads). LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED as pitched, because the benefit estimate does not survive contact with the target version. Reproducing the trigger over all 113 local transcripts (main thread, Bash-aware cat/sed -n/head/tail, Edit/Write -> full Read/cat of same path within 5 calls -> Edit within 5 calls) finds 20 loops total, 15 of them in ONE 2.1.251 session (docs project; 68 Edit/23 Write/28 Read on one file; loops in turns 2,3,6,18,28; ~83.5k tokens), 3 in a 2.1.247 session, 1 each in two 2.1.251/2.1.252 sessions, and ZERO in the 48 sessions on 2.1.269 (plus 0 in the 22 on 2.1.263). Two additional false-positive paths in the proposal: (1) basename matching — 8 basenames in the corpus are read/edited in 2–14 different directories (mod.rs/README.md-style collisions), so key on full path and display the basename; (2) "reads since last edit" ignores Bash-made edits — 1,704 of 4,699 Bash calls match sed -i/heredoc/tee/redirect, and auto mode explicitly instructs the model to edit via sed/heredocs, so a Bash write must reset the counter (use the same WRITE_COMMAND_MARKERS idea, plus staleReadFileStateHint presence) or the A04 signal fires on legitimate re-reads after a Bash edit.

C031.verdict: LENS 1 (data availability): NOT refuted. Every named source exists on this machine with the claimed meaning: Bash tool_use `input.command` on assistant lines; `toolUseResult.gitOperation` on 41 of 113 transcripts (228 results) with exactly the shapes {commit:{sha,kind,branch}}, {push:{branch}}, {pr:{number,url,action}}; `is_error` on tool_result blocks (parsed in src/transcript.rs:163, used by A15); PreToolUse arrives in the ~/.cctop/events spool with `tool_use_id` (hooks.rs:15) but `tool_input` is stripped at hooks.rs:75, so the pre-emptive trigger needs a bounded command summary kept, as the candidate says. Two data corrections: (a) `bashEditDiff` is present on 0 of 68 commit results, so the "files edited since last commit" list must come from tracked Edit/Write/MultiEdit calls (files.rs), not from the commit's diff; (b) the 30-char `input_summary` clip (src/tools.rs:53-80) loses the git verb on 132 of 580 commit-class commands (23%, `cd … && git commit` chains), so widening is mandatory, not optional. OTel vcs.* is optional/2.1.269-only. LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED on three counts. (1) Benefit estimate is inflated >10x. Replaying all 91 main-thread transcripts with the candidate's own trigger: 490 commit-class calls (not 548); 196 had a successful verify in the prior 10 calls, 176 had no edits at all in the window (commit-only turns), 118 fired — but 73 of those 118 edited only non-code files (md/PRD/yaml) which the candidate itself says to suppress, and 87 of 118 had a `git status/diff` in the window. After the candidate's own suppressions and one-shot-per-turn dedupe there are 7 distinct fires across 91 sessions (14 calls, 7 same-turn commit+push duplicates), all .py/.sh edits in 6 sessions — nowhere near "~180/month". Escalated case: 0 with the 3-call window, 4 with a 10-call window (candidate claims 5). "Commits every ~2 turns" is wrong: 182 of 796 user turns contain a commit-class call, but the median gap between consecutive commit-class calls is 0 turns (308 of 435 gaps) because commit→push→pr create chain inside one turn; without dedupe the rule would fire 2-3x per commit turn. (2) The pre-emptive "press Esc" action is not feasible: the hook spool shows PreToolUse→PostToolUse for git commands completing in 100 ms–1 s, and 1290 of 1427 permission-mode lines in local transcripts are `auto` (54 default), so the commit runs before a human can read two lines and reach Esc; the only real-time-able action is post-hoc ("reply: run the tests now, amend if red") or the one-time hook install, which is a settings nudge, not a live one. (3) The rework-cost argument is a non sequitur: the corpus has cargo 1, make 1, npm/pytest/tsc 0 failing test/build calls; the 58 git + 54 gh Bash errors are auth/repo/state plumbing failures (RW-05), not consequences of untested commits, so there is no local evidence of "unverified commit that breaks costs a fix turn". Not a duplicate of A01-A18 (A15 overlaps only the escalated wording). Wording as drafted is ~130 chars = 3 lines at 56 cols. FP rate after suppressions is acceptable (fires are genuine unverified code commits), but the rule is rare, post-hoc only, and its value is mostly captured by the turn-end "edits without a test run" rule (P01), which fires whether or not a commit follows.
C031.corrections: Trigger: keep commit|push|pr detection via gitOperation (post-hoc, exact) OR widened Bash command summary (>=80 chars, or a `git_verb` field extracted from the full command at parse time); require >=1 Edit/Write/MultiEdit on a code path (not md/txt/yaml/json/toml) since the last gitOperation.commit (not "last 10 calls" — window by commit boundary); no successful verify-class Bash (test|build|clippy|check|lint runners) since that boundary; fire once per turn (dedupe commit+push+pr chain); retire on next verify or next commit. Drop the PreToolUse pre-emptive path and the Esc instruction. Escalation: latest verify-class result is_error within the window since last commit (not 3 calls) — expect ~4 per 91 sessions. Wording (2 lines/56 cols): "Committed 3 code edits with no test/build run. / Reply: run the tests now; amend if anything is red." Escalated: "Committed after a FAILING check (exit 101). / Reply: fix the test, then amend the commit." Settings variant (fires once per session, first unverified commit): "Tip: PreToolUse hook on Bash(git commit:*) can run / the suite before every commit — see /hooks." Benefit estimate: ~7 distinct fires per 91 sessions (~1 per 13 sessions), 4 escalated; no measured rework cost locally — state as unquantified/best-practice-based. Priority: P2 (or fold into the turn-end P01 'edits without a check' rule, adding "and then committed" as a severity modifier). Keep gitOperation parsing as the A18 boundary input regardless.

My own per-turn pass over 816 main-thread turns: 118 turns contain an edit tool call, 81 of them (69%) edit only .md/.txt/.json/.yaml/.toml/.csv - the doc suppression is mandatory, not optional; 37 turns edit source files; 15 of those end with no verify-class Bash after the first edit (41%, ratio consistent with the phase model's 165/465, but that figure counts episodes incl. .md edits and sed -i and uses a wider 'verify' regex incl. description words like validate/confirm/passes). 13 of the 15 are also not verified in the next turn (so the nudge is not merely early). Amber-by-calls (>=14 calls after first edit, no verify) fires on 6 turns/month. Timing base: implement->first verify seconds n=291 p50 31 s p90 523 s, so a 10-min amber sits at ~p90 and will rarely fire on correct work. Command detection: only 9 of the 15 unverified source turns had a prior verify-class command in the session; the other 5 edited .sh/.tf/.html with no test command and only 1 of 5 CLAUDE.md files on this machine has a test line - the template '<detected test cmd>' would be empty ~1/3 of the time. Rework proxy: 3/15 unverified turns vs 1/22 verified turns were followed by a fix/error-worded prompt - directionally supportive, tiny n. No overlap with A01-A18 (A15 is same-args error loops, not a verification gap). Action is concrete and immediate (type 'run cargo test and fix failures before stopping' and Enter; or /goal). LENS 2 (actionability): REFUTED on benefit estimate and false-positive rate. The candidate's numbers are wrong: "25 corpus calls ran at 5m" is one session (c3254591); the corpus has 965 main-thread 5m calls. The breakeven claim ("one avoided 183k re-cache pays for ~9 turns of the 1h premium at an 892-token suffix write") ignores that cache writes on 5m periods averaged 3.07k tokens per call with many calls per turn: during the 5m periods the corpus wrote 2,965,294 cache tokens, of which only 763,436 (2 calls, both after 8-min gaps) were cold re-caches that a 1h TTL would have avoided (gaps > 60 min are cold on either TTL; the 22% ">5 min" figure from RW-09 includes those). At opus-5 list price ($5/M in; 5m write 1.25x, 1h write 2x, read 0.1x) the sessions actually on 5m cost $18.5 in writes; on 1h they would have cost (2.97M-763k)x$10/M + 763kx$0.5/M = $22.4, i.e. following the nudge would have cost $3.9 MORE. Per session, 1h wins only when cold re-cache tokens exceed ~39% of all cache-write tokens: true for 2 of 19 sessions (28c68a61 +$0.64, c3254591 +$0.70) and false for 17 — a nudge that fires on every flip is wrong ~90% of the time, far above the 1-in-5 tolerance. The subagent half is worse: 2.69M subagent 5m write tokens vs 178k cold after >5-min gaps (6.6%); subagentPromptCacheTtl 1h would have cost ~$8.5 more. The action itself is immediate and correct (settings.json promptCacheTtl / env CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL), the setting is honoured in overage, and the TTL flip does not invalidate the warm cache (the flip call in 28c68a61 wrote 4,386 and read 185,242), but the recommended remedy is net-negative for a typical session. C032.verdict: LENS 1 (data): NOT refuted, but the candidate mis-describes the sources. `toolUseResult.gitOperation` is real (plugin/.claude/types/claude-code.d.ts:8706 — commit{sha,kind:committed|amended|cherry-picked,branch?}, push{branch}, branch{ref,action:merged|rebased}, pr{number,url?,action}; d.ts comment: "Client-facing — lets clients render git activity without re-parsing stdout; not surfaced to the model") and appears on the tool_result user line as soon as the Bash call finishes, so it is live. In real transcripts it occurs on 231 Bash results (126 in 2026-08, 105 in 2026-09), of which 69 carry `commit` (45 commit-only, 22 commit+push, 2 commit without branch), 90 carry `push`, 100 carry `pr`, 4 `branch`. However cctop does not parse `toolUseResult` at all (`grep -rn toolUseResult src` → no hits), so "parsed, unconsumed" is wrong — it is unparsed. `git.rs` holds only branch+dirty (src/git.rs:7-30); numstat lives in `files.rs` and is diffed against the HEAD sha captured once at attach (src/attach.rs:45 `base_commit`, refreshed every 5 s at attach.rs:51-61), and `apply_numstat` (files.rs:90-107) keeps figures only for files Claude touched via Read/Edit/Write tool_use. So the existing "+a −d" is "since session start, Claude-touched files only" — it does not reset on commit, excludes untracked files and files changed by Bash/other tools (59 results carry `bashEditDiff`), and would be wrong for the claimed "uncommitted since last commit" line. Commits made outside Claude Code (another terminal/session, `gh pr merge`) emit no gitOperation, so the edits/minutes counter cannot key off gitOperation alone. All of this is computable with the shell-out cctop already does: `git diff --numstat HEAD` (+ `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` for untracked, `git status --porcelain` count for files), `git rev-parse HEAD` to detect HEAD change (reset counter) and `git log -1 --format=%ct` for minutes-since-commit — verified in this repo. LENS 2 (actionability): NOT refuted. It is a passive Files-panel line, not a nudge, so the 1-in-5 false-positive rule does not apply; it does not duplicate A01–A18 (A18 explicitly has no boundary/commit detection, rules.rs has no git reference); the action (type "commit"/run the user's commit skill, or judge /rewind blast radius) is immediate. But the benefit estimate is inflated: "222 git operations/month" is actually 231 over two months and only 69 are commits; "commits happen every ~2 turns" is false — 816 user turns / 69 commits ≈ 12 turns per commit, and within-session median gap between commits is 426 s (p25 118 s, p75 2013 s, n=42) with a median of 2 edit calls between commits (p75 5, max 44, n=68). For this user the checkpoint habit already exists most of the time; the value is in the tail (≥ 5 edits or ≥ 30 min uncommitted). The proposed wording is 72 chars, over the 56-column limit.

The fallback path IS verified: 58 gaps > 60 min inside single transcripts (Aug 12 - Sep 13, 113 transcripts); the first API call after the gap had cache_creation > 50 % of context in 55/58, and 50 of those had ctx > 100k (samples cc 836,644 / cr 29,377 after 506 min; 685,648 after 281 min). 12,318 of 13,315 assistant usages report ephemeral_1h_input_tokens > 0, so the 1 h TTL threshold (agg.observed_ttl, src/metrics/usage.rs:305) is the right one.
